method: Read-only local inputs; no source manifest rebinding, rebuild, or installation.

Current top-level and recursively nested JAR assets/data; KubeJS same-path overrides. Deterministic filename order is not runtime collision evidence. Selected external resource packs are not treated as upstream.
Historical global language inventory omitted some nested/developer/project-generated keys. Newly observed keys are review candidates, not proven version additions or missing translations.
Markdown text hashes normalize CRLF/CR to LF; Patchouli uses raw UTF-8 hashes, matching historical extraction.
Full old mod inventory unavailable; missing historical language-source filenames show rebinding needs, not a total updated-mod count. Official historical API returned HTTP 403.

old: Every cast costs mana and adds burnout. Run short of either and the spell fails.
Bake a &aMana Cake&r for a long boost to Mana Regeneration. A &2Mana Martini&r lowers burnout for a while, and mana potions come in six strengths; JEI lists them all.
Your mana pool grows by 25 with every magic level, so leveling is the long-term answer.
new: Every cast costs mana and adds burnout. Run short of either and the spell fails.
Bake a &aMana Cake&r for a long boost to Mana Regeneration. A &2Mana Martini&r lowers burnout for a while, and mana potions come in six strengths; JEI lists them all.
Your mana pool grows by 50 with every magic level, so leveling is the long-term answer.

old: The &dPurifier&r allows you to remove &5Enchantments&r and &cCurses&r from items using blood.
You'll need at least 1 bucket's worth of blood in the &dPurifier&r, then throw in the item you want to remove an enchantment from and a &cBlook&r to absorb one of the enchants from the item.
new: The &dPurifier&r allows you to remove &5Enchantments&r and &cCurses&r from items using blood.

To remove an &5Enchantment&r, fill the &dPurifier&r with 3 buckets of blood, then right-click it with the item you want to disenchant and with a &cBlook&r. One random enchantment is moved onto the &cBlook&r, which becomes an &5Enchanted Book&r, and all 3 buckets are used up.
To remove a &cCurse&r, you only need 1 bucket of blood and the cursed item; no &cBlook&r is needed. Each curse level removed uses 1 bucket. Curses on the &4Vengeance Pickaxe&r can't be removed.
Every &aCrafting Storage&r and &aCo-Processor&r in a &eNodeworks&r CPU makes &bheat&r, and more of it when packed against other CPU parts. When your coolant can't keep up, the CPU slows down.
&aCoolants&r count as part of the CPU, so you can use them to link parts together.
Any coolant touching a CPU block cools it, and each one gets a &bcluster bonus&r for every other coolant next to it. A solid wall of coolant works far better than single blocks spread around.
{@pagebreak}
&aCrafting Coolant&r: 1 cooling, +1 per neighboring coolant
&3Adamantite Coolant&r: 2 cooling, +2 per neighboring coolant
&dAeternium Coolant&r: 3 cooling, +3 per neighboring coolant
&6Aurichalcum Coolant&r: 4 cooling, +4 per neighboring coolant
A single layer of &3Adamantite Coolant&r against your CPU is enough to fully cool any part of it. Higher tiers do the same job with fewer blocks.

old: Ammunition runs out. Your network usually does not.

Infuse an &cEnchanted Bullet Modifier&r on a Tier I Ara Vitae to make a &cBlood Bullet&r, then slot it into a gun. Each shot draws 50 EV from your network in place of a bullet, so the gun fires even with an empty magazine.
When the network cannot pay, the gun falls back on whatever bullets are loaded.
new: Ammunition runs out. Your network usually does not.

Infuse an &cEnchanted Bullet Modifier&r on a Tier I Ara Vitae to make a &cBlood Bullet&r, then slot it into a gun. Each shot draws 50 EV from your network in place of a bullet, so the gun reloads even if you don't have bullets.
When the network cannot pay, the gun falls back on whatever bullets you have to reload with.

Sacrificed blood that arrives faster than the basin can hold is not lost. It pools in an [#](8B0000)overflow reserve[#]() holding up to [#](8B0000)twenty times[#]() the basin's capacity, and flows back into the basin each tick as room opens.\
\
A great offering from a [#](8B0000)Well of Suffering[#]() or a [#](8B0000)Torment Nexus[#]() can therefore feed an altar whose basin is far smaller than the offering itself. A [#](8B0000)Seer's Sigil[#]() reveals what waits in the reserve.
